title: Ammonium Carbonicum
text: This remedy is characterized by a general lack of vital force and a tendency to decomposition. It is useful in cases of extreme debility, particularly in people with a sedentary lifestyle. There is a general feeling of heaviness and tiredness. The patient is often a stout, elderly person. There is a marked tendency to haemorrhages and a feeling of chilliness. Confused and forgetful. Depression and anxiety. Fears death. Aversion to work. Headache, with a sensation of weight in the forehead. Vertigo on rising. Scalp feels tight. Eyes red and burning. Dimness of vision. Double vision. Chronic catarrh of the nose. Dryness and obstruction. Sneezing. Nosebleed. Expression of pain and anxiety. Pale and sallow. Redness of the face. Dryness of the mouth. Tongue feels dry and sticky. Foul breath. Toothache. Dryness and rawness in the throat. Swollen and sore. Sensation of a lump in the throat. Appetite poor. Thirst. Heaviness and pressure after eating. Eructations. Distended with gas. Rumbling. Flatulence. Constipation. Stool large and hard. Haemorrhoids, with burning and itching. Frequent desire to urinate. Scanty urine. Menses profuse and early. Leucorrhoea. Shortness of breath on motion. Violent cough, with a sensation of oppression in the chest. Hoarseness. Palpitation, with a sensation of oppression in the region of the heart. Aching and lameness in the limbs. Heaviness in the legs. Trembling of the hands. Itching and burning. Dry and scaly. Eruptions like miliary rash. Worse from cold air and in the morning. Better from warmth and in the open air. Compare: Lachesis; Rhus toxicodendron; Arsenicum album. Third to thirtieth potency.
